facts.text: The 2024 movie The Fall Guy features a fake movie-within-the-movie called "Metalstorm", directly based on this film's props, sets, characters and costumes.
Charles Band shot this in 3-D partly to land a Universal deal: the studio was releasing Jaws 3-D and wanted a second 3-D picture to send out with it.
Per Charles Band, Metalstorm cost about $900,000 to shoot, and Universal bought distribution rights for $3 million.
Richard Moll shaved his head for Hurok. Night Court's producers liked the look and cast him as bald bailiff Bull Shannon, a role he played for years.
Kelly Preston was first billed as Kelly Palzis. According to Charles Band, she picked the Preston stage name halfway through production.
Richard Band composed and recorded the whole score in just eleven days.
Demi Moore auditioned for the role of Dhyana, the part that went to Kelly Preston.
Jared-Syn is played by Mike Preston, who had been in Mad Max 2 (The Road Warrior). Critics called the film "Star Wars meets Mad Max".
The names are deliberate: Dogen was a 13th-century Zen master, and "dhyana" is the Sanskrit word for deep meditative concentration, which Japanese renders as "Zen".
The tagline "It's High Noon at the End of the Universe" nods to the 1952 western High Noon. Band reused it for Oblivion 2: Backlash.
Grandmaster Steven Judson Silverfox II trained the lead actors for several months in Shinpu Ren Karate and GD Jujitsu, which were used in many of the fight scenes.
Many of the road-warrior vehicles were scrappy builds, reportedly sheet metal mounted on VW chassis. A reviewer called the look "lo-fi".
Principal photography began in February 1982 and ran seven weeks, in Simi Valley and at Vasquez Rocks, with Mac Ahlberg shooting. Ahlberg also shot the earlier 3-D film Parasite.
Band and co-producer Alan J. Adler worked for deferred pay as the film's scope and budget grew beyond a simple follow-up to their earlier 3-D film Parasite.
A video game tie-in was planned but never made. Charles Band even shot extra footage to connect the film to it.
Adler wrote in lots of Native American mythology and Atlantis legend, hoping to develop it in a planned trilogy. The film earned too little to justify sequels.
Jeffrey Byron is John Ford's godson and the son of actress Anna Lee.
Tim Thomerson came from stand-up comedy and made it to The Tonight Show. This was his first film for Charles Band, and he later did nine films with Albert Pyun.
Byron and Moll returned for Band's 1984 film The Dungeonmaster, which also reused some of these road-warrior vehicles.
Critics weren't kind. The New York Times called it "slow-moving, thoroughly derivative", and CinemaScore audiences gave it a D-.
In Japan the film came out in 3-D on the short-lived VHD disc format. That disc was widely copied for bootleg tapes and DVDs.
The 2016 Scream Factory Blu-ray includes a 42-minute making-of, "High Noon at the End of the Universe", with Band, Byron, Moll and Thomerson, though not Kelly Preston.
Metalstorm opened August 19, 1983, four weeks after Jaws 3-D, which it was meant to play alongside.
